quote: Seven peptide regions (domains 1-7) containing 178 amino acids were found to be common to all elements.
note: The origin of the seven-way numbered partition in the held evidence set. A block count and a total length, on an alignment; no residue coordinates for any individual block.

quote: conserved residues present in each RT sequence were used to identify the seven domains. Alignment of residues between these fixed positions was by the Unitary Matrix (UM) method
note: The stated construction method: fixed conserved residues first, alignment between them second. This is a reproducible procedure, not a drawn boundary.

quote: we have identified 42 conserved positions that contain identical or chemically similar residues in the majority of the 82 RT sequences analyzed in this report
note: The conserved-position evidence underlying the blocks, with its own denominator of 82 sequences.

quote: To be classified as a conserved position the residues had to be present in over 50% of the RT elements from three of the four most abundant groups of RT-containing elements
note: An explicit, quantitative, restatable inclusion criterion. This is the textual-criteria route of launcher section 5e, and it succeeds.

quote: In the case of Poch et al. (1989) the five motifs identified (regions a-e) correspond to our domains 3-7.
note: The stated correspondence between the Poch motif partition and the numbered partition; the cross-walk is the authors own, not this project's.

quote: In the case of Webster et al. (1989) the four blocks identified correspond to our domains 2-5.
note: A second independent confirmation, for a different subset of the series.

quote: Thus of the seven shared domains shown in Figure 1 only domain 1 has not been independently confirmed.
note: The authors own statement that one of the seven carries weaker support than the rest. Retained because it is the block a later concordance failure would most plausibly involve.

quote: Most of the RNA viruses did not have a complete domain 6, a situation similar to the RT elements of the copia/Tyl group.
note: Whole element classes lack a complete block. Block absence was a described phenomenon in 1990, not a detector artefact introduced later.

quote: The RT domain forms the bulk of the ORF and consists of subdomains 1-7 [palm and finger regions in the crystal structure of HIV-RT (6)]
note: The subdomain numbering, stated as composition and mapped to structure by analogy. Naming plus an analogy is not a boundary.

quote: Subdomain 0 can be considered an N-terminal extension of the RT domain and is conserved among non-LTR RTs.
note: Subdomain 0 introduced as an extension of the domain rather than as a member of the series.

quote: [Domain 0 was formerly called domain Z but was more recently renamed domain 0 in non-LTR RTs (7)]
note: The rename that makes the RT0 concept older than its name, and attributes it to a source outside the held set.

quote: are labeled according to previous studies (7,9,32) taking into account the boundaries of conservation seen in our alignment
note: The labels are inherited from three earlier papers. This single sentence is why the numbering has to be traced rather than read off.

quote: taking into account the boundaries of conservation seen in our alignment
note: The same sentence also states that the inherited labels were adjusted against this paper's own alignment, which is the alignment acquired in this gate as ALIGN_000044.

quote: subdomain 0 is conserved only between group II intron and non-LTR RTs
note: The scope statement the launcher treats as load-bearing. Verified at the PDF in this gate rather than inherited from the prior dossier. It bounds where the concept applies; it is not a residue boundary.

quote: subdomain 2A is weakly conserved among non-LTR, group II intron and retron RTs
note: The companion scope statement, and the only held Tier-1 sentence that names retron RTs and a numbered region together.

quote: These sites are between subdomains 4 and 5 of the RT domain (the 4/5 spacer) and between subdomain 7 and domain X (the 7/X spacer)
note: Two named regions defined by what they lie between, with stated length ranges. Defining a gap is not defining the blocks on either side of it.

quote: Domain X (analogous to the thumb structure of HIV-RT)
note: Domain X named and mapped to the thumb by analogy.

quote: RT subdomains 0-7 are equally conserved within each of the mitochondrial and bacterial groups (90 and 94 residues respectively)
note: A count of conserved residues over the whole series, per group. A total for the series is not a per-block extent.

quote: The presence of a catalytic YxDD motif in subdomain 5 of the RT.
note: Places the catalytic motif in a named block; the single most transferable landmark in the held set.

quote: RT domains 1-7 constitute the palm and finger domains of the polymerase protein, and their sequences are generally alignable across RTs
note: The published sequence-to-structure mapping. Reported and testable in this track; never assumed.

quote: In contrast, domains 0 and 2a are shared among only a subset of RT classes
note: The second independent line, in a different paper, for treating 0 and 2a as scope-limited rather than as series members.

quote: Downstream of the RT domain is domain X, which corresponds to the thumb of the polymerase
note: Domain X mapped to the thumb, restated seven years after Zimmerly 2001.

quote: retrons have fewer alignable characters than group II introns (157 versus 177), DGRs have about the same number (179 versus 177) and five other groups have fewer alignable characters (126-167 amino acids)
note: The only published measurement of how far the numbered frame transfers across classes, and the external benchmark this track's per-class occupancy improves on. Retrons are the hard case.

quote: domains 1, 2 and 7 are unalignable for many bacterial RTs, while obviously present in most eukaryotic RTs
note: Named blocks that already fail to transfer within bacteria in the published literature. A non-detection in these blocks was predicted in 2008.

quote: in the Y/FxDD motif of the catalytic site, the x is nearly always hydrophobic (A, I, V and M), whereas the bacterial group AbiP2 has a conserved R
note: The registered trap D10, verified at the source: the hydrophobic statement is about position 2 of the motif, and an excluded class differs elsewhere.

quote: with only 59 amino acids alignable across the entire set
note: The floor of transferability across all bacterial RT classes. The running text does not say which blocks those 59 characters fall in.

quote: Four consensus sequences are conserved with the same linear arrangement in RNA-dependent DNA polymerases encoded by retroid elements and in RNA-dependent RNA polymerases
note: The motif partition that predates the numbered one, defined by consensus sequences and linear order.

quote: These consensus sequences altogether lead to 4 strictly and 18 conservatively maintained amino acids embedded in a large domain of 120 to 210 amino acids.
note: Residue-level evidence and a stated span for the containing domain, not for the individual motifs.

quote: an overall domain which encompasses four (A to D) out of the five initial RT-motifs conserved in the same linear arrangement
note: The fifth RT-motif exists in this paper's own vocabulary but is outside the four it establishes; this is the sentence that reconciles four motifs with the five that Xiong & Eickbush cite.

quote: for motif C with two invariant Asp residues
note: The catalytic core of the motif partition, which is also the catalytic core of the numbered one.

quote: a reverse transcriptase domain (residues 261-886)
note: The only stated coordinate boundary in the authors own alignment: the RT domain as a whole, in alignment columns, with no internal subdivision.

quote: PILEUP, CLUSTALX and manual adjustment
note: The stated construction method of the primary alignment, including a manual step that is not reproducible from the record.

quote: the RT domain contains conserved sequence motifs RT1-RT7 found in the fingers and palm of retroviral RTs, along with an upstream motif RT0 characteristic of the RTs of non-LTR-retroelements
note: The modern RT0-RT7 spelling in the held set, used with citations to the three earlier sources and no new derivation of its own.

quote: a 10-kDa N-terminal fragment containing RT0 (M1-R85)
note: A residue-coordinate boundary, but on one protein and from proteolysis, not from sequence conservation. It may constrain or falsify a sequence-defined edge; it may not manufacture one.

quote: insertions 2a, 3a, 4a, and 7a relative to HIV-1 RT
note: 2a appears here as one of a series of insertions relative to a reference structure, which is a different object from Zimmerly's weakly conserved subdomain 2A.

quote: less conserved in the algal group (15 positions) and poorly conserved in the bacterial group (five positions)
note: Per-group conserved-position counts for domain X out of 105 positions, which is block-level conservation evidence rather than naming. It is also the sentence that shows the same region can be well conserved in one group and nearly absent in another - the pattern this track must not read as a detector failure.
